tagline: Korea's island-studded inner sea — a protected marine park of dramatic islets where the only way between them is a diesel excursion ferry.
summary: The Hallyeo coast — Yeosu, Tongyeong, Namhae, Hansan — is Korea's only true scenic archipelago, a calm Setouchi-like inner sea protected since 1968 as Hallyeohaesang, the country's first marine national park. It draws over a million visitors a year to islet-hopping, the Yeosu Expo 2012 waterfront, and a wave of new resorts (Hilton Yeosu, Stanford Tongyeong). The distances between these jewels are short and the water is sheltered — an almost purpose-built all-electric island-hopping network, and a chance to take diesel exhaust out of a born-protected marine park.

use_cases.title: Hallyeo islet-hopping network
use_cases.body: Frequent all-electric foiling shuttles knit Yeosu, Odongdo, Hansan-do, Tongyeong and the Namhae islets into a smooth island-hopping circuit — replacing slow, fixed-schedule diesel excursion ferries through the protected park.

use_cases.title: Resort-coast transfers
use_cases.body: Direct foiling arrivals to the new Hilton Yeosu, Stanford Tongyeong and Hidden Bay jetties give premium guests a smooth water transfer between coastal towns and island resorts.

use_cases.title: Yeosu ↔ Tongyeong coastal link
use_cases.body: A fast cross-bay foiling service connects the two anchor cities and the towns between them across the calm inner sea, turning a long coastal drive into a short, scenic hop.

navier_fit.pioneer_ii: This is a Pioneer II archipelago through and through: short, sheltered hops between Yeosu, Odongdo, Hansan-do, Tongyeong and the Namhae islets, plus the ~35 nm Yeosu↔Tongyeong link — all well inside the 70 nm all-electric range and ideally suited to the calm inner sea.
navier_fit.quanta_lr: Reserved for the longer connectors out of the park — line-hauls toward Busan-Geoje to the east or the Jeju link to the south — and for the quiet-mode, refuel-anywhere reliability that suits a born-protected marine-park brand without building shoreside charging at every small island.

competitive_landscape: Movement through the Hallyeo park today is by conventional excursion and car ferries run by local operators, plus coastal roads and bridges. The boats are diesel, fixed-schedule and weather-limited, and they run through one of Korea's most protected seascapes. That established, year-round islet-hopping traffic is the demand base; a clean foiling network upgrades the experience and the park's environmental footprint at once.
seasonality: The inner sea is unusually calm and workable across most of the year — a Setouchi-like sheltered analog — with the main disruption being the summer typhoon season (roughly Jul–Sep). Foiling's smoother ride extends comfortable operating days through the shoulder seasons and offers reliability when the open approaches kick up.
regulatory_note: Operations run within Hallyeohaesang National Park under the Korea National Park Service (KNPS) and across two provincial jurisdictions (Jeollanam-do and Gyeongsangnam-do), with the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries on maritime rules. The marine-park status makes a zero-local-emission, low-wake foiling fleet a strong fit for conservation-aligned permitting and the 2025–28 greenfield resort design-in window.
